novel_features.name: Cross-index search
novel_features.description: Search across every synced index in one shot, with each hit labeled by its source index.
novel_features.rationale: No single Algolia API endpoint spans indices; only a local SQLite store can query multiple synced indices at once.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when you need to know which of your indices contains a record, without issuing N API calls.

novel_features.name: Settings diff
novel_features.description: Field-level comparison of settings between two indices (or a settings file vs an index).
novel_features.rationale: Requires local snapshots of settings to compare; the API only returns one index's settings at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to verify prod/staging parity before a release instead of exporting and eyeballing JSON.

novel_features.name: Stale rules report
novel_features.description: Find rules that reference attributes missing from the index's searchable attributes or that can never match.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining local rules with the index settings; no API endpoint cross-checks rules against settings.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to find dead-weight relevance rules before they silently corrupt search results.

novel_features.name: API key ACL report
novel_features.description: Audit all API keys: write-capable, unrestricted, and expired keys grouped by ACL, with last-use from synced logs.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local aggregation of keys plus log activity; the API returns keys and logs separately.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for key rotation audits to catch write-capable keys that have gone unused for months.

novel_features.name: Search regression check
novel_features.description: Assert that a query returns expected objectIDs, with a typed exit code for CI pipelines.
novel_features.rationale: Adds an assertion contract and exit-code semantics over the live search endpoint that no existing tool provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this after every rule or synonym change to catch relevance regressions before they reach users.

novel_features.name: Unsearchable-records report
novel_features.description: List records missing attributes required by the index's searchable settings — records search can never return.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining local records with the index settings to find records with null/empty required attributes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this after catalog imports to find records that are silently unreachable by search.

novel_features.name: Records diff between indices
novel_features.description: Compare records of two indices (added/removed/changed by objectID) to verify prod/staging parity.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local records tables for both indices joined on objectID; the API has no cross-index comparison.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to reconcile dev and prod copies after a copy/move operation instead of exporting and diffing files.

novel_features.name: Logs error digest
novel_features.description: Aggregate synced log entries by error code and link failed tasks for a digest of what went wrong.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local aggregation of log entries joined with the tasks table; the API returns raw log lines only.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for weekly error triage to see error spikes and affected indices at a glance.

narrative.headline: Every Algolia feature, plus offline search and a local database no other Algolia tool has.
narrative.value_prop: The Algolia CLI manages indices, records, search, rules, synonyms, API keys, and settings from the terminal — with a local SQLite mirror, cross-index search, settings diffing, and relevance regression checks that the official CLI cannot offer.
narrative.auth_narrative: Algolia uses two credentials: your Application ID (ALGOLIA_APPLICATION_ID) and an API key (ALGOLIA_API_KEY), sent as x-algolia-application-id and x-algolia-api-key headers. Find both in the Algolia dashboard under Settings > API Keys. Export them before running the CLI.

quickstart.comment: Verify your Algolia credentials are set and the API is reachable.
See every index in your application with record counts and sizes.
Search an index with the same parameters as the dashboard.
Mirror your index list into the local SQLite store for offline queries.
Search across all synced indices at once.

troubleshoots.fix: Check the index name — list indices with: algolia-pp-cli indices list

troubleshoots.symptom: HTTP 403 'API key has no ACLs to perform this action'
troubleshoots.fix: Use a key with the required ACL (search, browse, settings, etc.) from the dashboard.
Algolia rate limits per key — retry after a few seconds or use a key with higher quota.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you manage Algolia indices, records, rules, synonyms, or API keys from the terminal, or when you need offline access to your Algolia data for scripts, CI, and agent workflows.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for Algolia Analytics or Recommend product APIs — those are separate products with their own hosts.
Do not use this CLI as a full dashboard replacement for complex merchandising visual workflows.

recipes.title: Verify a relevance change
recipes.explanation: Assert that a query still returns an expected hit — run in CI after every rule or synonym change.

recipes.title: Find dead rules
recipes.explanation: Surface rules that reference removed attributes or can never match.

recipes.title: Compare prod and staging settings
recipes.explanation: See exactly which settings differ between two indices before a release.

recipes.title: Cross-index lookup
recipes.explanation: Find which synced index contains a record and narrow the output with --select.

recipes.title: Audit API keys
recipes.explanation: Get a permission matrix of write-capable, unrestricted, and expired keys.
